hook: The Stone House of 1873, from India Basin's first generation of scow-schooner builders.

historical_record.description: The Stone House was built — one of three structures surviving from the earliest era of wooden boat building at India Basin.

William Stone moved his boat yard from Potrero Point to 9th (Innes) Avenue near G (Griffith) Street, following Johnson J. Dircks to the shallow northern shoreline of the Hunters Point peninsula, where immigrant shipwrights built shallow-draft bay scows for over fifty years. The yards were family-run and often home-based, the builders' dwellings standing among the boat lofts and storage sheds, and the craft passed from father to son for three generations.
